terms.comment: The general word for anything given for merit, a prize as much as a reward (see reward). To award one is praemium dare or tribuere (Cic. Arch. 25), to offer one prōpōnere (Caes. BC 1.17), to win one cōnsequī (Caes. BG 1.42; Lewis & Short). First prize is praemium prīmārium, second secundārium (Traupman 365).

terms.gloss: the palm of victory, first prize
evidence: Cic. Brut. 173: cum palmam jam prīmus accēperit (Lewis & Short)
Varr. RR 3.16.14: Siculum mel fert palmam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First the palm of the hand and the palm tree; a palm branch was given to victors from 293 BC (Livy), so the prize and the victory itself: palmam ferre, to take first prize, palmam dare, dēferre alicui, to award it. A champion has multae palmae (Cic. Rosc. Am. 17).

evidence: Tert. adv. Marc. 3; Prud. Perist. 5.538 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Greek word, from Christian writers; Saint Paul’s runners race for it.

phrases.latin: cūnctī adsint meritaeque exspectent praemia palmae
phrases.english: let everyone be there and wait for the prizes they have earned

phrases.latin: praemium solvendae quaestiōnis pōnēbat librum veteris scrīptōris vel Graecum vel Latīnum et corōnam ē laurō plexam
phrases.english: as the prize for solving a question he offered a book by an old writer, Greek or Latin, and a crown woven of bay

phrases.latin: Nescītis quod iī quī in stadiō currunt, omnēs quidem currunt, sed ūnus accipit bravium?
phrases.english: Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize?

sources: Lewis & Short: praemium · Lewis & Short: palma · Lewis & Short: brabeum
